why: Same mathematics in two models. A: on the matrix model with its slice structure, height_param (f∘param k = c_k + Σ(c_j−c_k)(x_j²+y_j²) on the closed ball), critical points = param k 0, non-degenerate of index 2#{c_j<c_k}, f Morse, rank bijective, C_λ = 1 for λ = 0,2,…,2n. B: on the quotient model, for EVERY smooth structure in which Milnor's coordinates are diffeomorphisms onto the ball, the same six claims. A ⇒ B: compute in the coordinate system Φ_k (from B's hypothesis, IsSmoothCoord); f∘Φ_k⁻¹ is Milnor's model by A's height_param, then the project's model lemmas (outside A) give critical points/non-degeneracy/index, and the count uses A's bijective_rank. B ⇒ A: B's hypotheses are satisfiable (Milnor atlas built from the project's V3_41 lemmas); B's conclusions are transported to the slice structure through x ↦ x xᴴ, both sides computed in Milnor's coordinates (a slice-side IsSmoothCoord for coord k); bijective_rank is derived from B's count. Only height_param (an algebraic identity, also on the sphere nsq z = 1 outside U_k, beyond Milnor's U_k formula) is re-proved outright.
